tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

# edit.json (EDL) reference

Implementation: `studio/mcstudio/edl.py` (timing), `render.py` (compiler), `captions.py` (ASS).

## Time

- **Output time** `at`: seconds in the finished video.
- **Source time** `src_at`: seconds in the raw gameplay recording, which is what the transcript and signals use. **Prefer `src_at`.** It survives re-cutting, and it is dropped with a warning if that footage was cut.
- Inside a segment, `zoom` and `shake` take `src_at`, or `at` relative to the segment's own start.

## Anchors (pick one per event)
- `"seg": "s012", "src_at": 312.4`: source time **inside that segment**. This is the preferred anchor, and shorts carry
  it along.
- `"seg": "s012", "rel": 0.5`: seconds after that segment starts. Negative values are allowed, e.g. -0.29 for a stinger.
- `"src_at": 312.4`: source seconds. Ambiguous when the same footage appears twice, as in cold opens.
- `"at": 61.2`: output seconds. Avoid this one, because it breaks whenever the cut changes.

## Top level

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1, "project": "ep01", "title": "...",
  "max_rating": "mild",              // optional: video-wide ceiling for mcs check
  "format": "landscape",             // or "vertical" (1080x1920 shorts)
  "mode": "funny",                   // default mode for segments without one (studio/modes.json)
  "look": "clean",                   // base colour polish (studio/looks.json)
  "facecam": {"layout": "corner"},   // needs sources.facecam; vertical defaults to "stack"
  "avatar": {"always": false},       // narration avatar; also on automatically in narration mode
  "watermark": {"text": "@NAME", "opacity": 0.55},
  "guard_cuts": true,                // render-time protection against clipped words
  "shorts": [{"from": "s010", "to": "s014", "hook": "HE TRIED..."}],   // optional hints for mcs shorts
  "style": { },                      // optional deep-override of studio/style.json
  "sources": { },                    // optional override of project.json sources
  "segments": [ ],                   // main timeline, back to back
  "overlays": [ ],                   // composited over the timeline
  "text": [ ],                       // animated text pops (libass)
  "audio": { "sfx": [ ], "music": [ ], "bleeps": [ ] },
```

## segments

| type | required | optional |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `in`, `out` (source s) | `speed` (0.25–4; atempo keeps pitch), `zoom[]`, `shake[]`, `effects[]`, `freeze_end` (s), `mute_game`, `mute_mic`, `game_db`, `mic_db`, `mode`, `look`, `exact`, `facecam` (false hides), `avatar`, `avatar_mood`, `header_text` (pov), `frame_x` (vertical crop pan 0..1) |
| `cutaway` | `asset` or `file` | `in`, `out` (asset s; defaults to the asset's `use_window`), `volume_db`, `mute`, `blur_bg` (default true), `effects[]`, `freeze_end` |
| `card` | `file` (pre-rendered mp4/mov) + `dur`, **or** `template` + `vars` (channel motion graphic, rendered opaque) | `effects[]` |

**zoom item:** `{"src_at": 312.4, "to": 1.35, "in": 0.12, "hold": 0.8, "out": 0.18, "focus": [0.5, 0.45]}`
- `to` is the scale factor (1.15 subtle, 1.3 punch, 1.6+ dramatic).
- `in` / `out` are ramp seconds. `0` = snap (hard punch-in or snap-back). If `hold` is omitted, the zoom holds until the segment ends.
- `focus` is the normalized point to zoom toward. Crosshair = [0.5, 0.5]. A mob on the left ≈ [0.3, 0.5].

**shake item:** `{"src_at": 312.4, "dur": 0.4, "amp": 14, "freq": 18}`. `amp` is in px at 1080p.

**effects:** `flash` (white flash-in), `bw`, `deepfry`, `vignette`, `sepia`, `invert`, `brighten` (lift dark cave/underwater footage). These apply to the whole segment, so split segments to scope them.

## overlays

Common fields: `type`, `asset` | `file`, `at` | `src_at`, `in` (source offset into the asset), `dur`, `x`, `y` (0–1 center), `scale` (fraction of frame height), `flip`, `rotate` (deg), `opacity`, `audio` (bool, default true for video), `volume_db`, `key_mode` (override), `key_color`, `similarity`, `blend`.

| type | notes |
|---|---|
| `greenscreen` | Keyed with the asset's sampled `key_color` (green/blue/black_screen auto). Default `scale` 0.45. Use `placement` `fullscreen` for full-frame effects. |
| `video` | Same as greenscreen but for alpha (`.mov` ProRes 4444) or unkeyed picture-in-picture. |
| `image` | Sticker. `anim` defaults to `pop` (scale 0 → 115% → 100%); use `"anim": "none"` for static. Default `dur` 1.2, `scale` 0.3. GIFs animate. |
| `motion` | `template` + `vars` from the channel motion library (rendered and cached automatically), or `file` for your own HyperFrames .mov. |
| `transition` | Full-screen wipe. `at` / `src_at` = **the cut point**, and the wipe starts `cover_s` earlier (default half its length). Check asset `notes` for the real cover time. Place it exactly on a segment boundary. |

## text

`{"text": "-1 DIAMOND", "src_at": 401.2, "dur": 1.2, "style": "minecraft", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.3, "anim": "pop", "size": 120, "color": "#55FF55", "rotate": -5}`

Styles (in studio/style.json):
- `impact` — big white Luckiest Guy
- `minecraft` — Minecraft Ten with grey shadow
- `label` — small yellow Minecraft UI text, slides in
- `danger` — red, shakes
- `retro` — VCR
- `gta` — Pricedown gold, "WASTED"-style

`anim` can be `pop`, `slide`, `shake` or `none`.

When defining a new text style, the font must be the font's **name-table family (ID 1)**, otherwise libass silently falls back to Arial:
- Luckiest Guy
- Minecraft / Minecraft Ten / Minecraft Five

- LEMON MILK Bold

## audio

- **sfx:** `{"asset": "sfx_ui.vine-boom", "src_at": 401.2, "align": "peak", "volume_db": -2, "in": 0.0, "dur": 1.0}`
  - `align: "peak"` (the default for role `hit`) lands the asset's loudest moment exactly on the time. `"onset"` (the default otherwise) starts the sound at the time. Leading silence is trimmed automatically from the catalog's onset analysis.
- **music:** `{"asset": "music.x", "at": 0, "until": 95.0, "in": 12.0, "volume_db": 0, "fade_in": 0.5, "fade_out": 1.5, "duck": true}`
  - The track loops if it's shorter than the span. `duck` sidechain-compresses it under the voice. Swap tracks at mood changes, with overlapping fades.
- **bleeps:** `{"src_at": 233.9, "dur": 0.4}` mutes dialogue and plays a 1 kHz tone. Find the swear's word timing in `transcript.json`.

**Levels are automatic. Don't hand-balance.** Every SFX, music bed, overlay and cutaway is gain-staged *relative to the creator's voice*, using the same "loud moments" metric on both sides:
- The asset side is the catalog `loud_db`.
- The voice side is the processed voice measured inside transcript words.

The targets per role are in `style.json` → `audio.mix.sfx_rel_db`: hit -6, whoosh -10, voice_line -4, stinger -6, ambience -12, music -18 dB under the voice. `volume_db` on an event is only a *nudge* on top (±2–3 dB): use it for taste, never to fix loudness.

The SFX bus also ducks ~3 dB while the creator talks. If the recording has voice and game on **one track**, the track is pulled down `game_between_words_db` (-8) between words. To quiet loud game noise in a stretch without speech (e.g. a death screen), set `"mic_db": -10` on that segment.

The final mix gets a static gain to -14 LUFS plus a -1.5 dBFS peak limiter (not `loudnorm`, which silently compresses).

```jsonc
"captions": {
```

244	                for k in range(i, j + 1):
245	                    if run >= 4.0:
246	                        final[k].setdefault("effects", []).append("brighten")
247	                i = j + 1
248	            else:
249	                i += 1
250	        return final

252	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ 3. modes
253	    STORY_MODES = {"panic": "scary", "jumpscare": "scary", "death": "sad"}

255	    def assign_modes(self, segs: list[dict], beats: list[dict]) -> None:
256	        """The look stays in the base mode. It only changes for a real story SECTION: 8+ s of scary
257	        (panic/jumpscare run) or the sad ending after a death. Per-beat mood flips were unwatchable."""
258	        dur = lambda s: (s["out"] - s["in"]) / s.get("speed", 1)  # noqa: E731
259	        cand = []
260	        for s in segs:
261	            inside = [b for b in beats if s["in"] - 0.2 <= b["t"] < s["out"] and b["score"] >= 4]
262	            m = next((self.STORY_MODES[b["moment"]] for b in sorted(inside, key=lambda b: -b["score"])
263	                      if b["moment"] in self.STORY_MODES), None)
264	            cand.append(m)
265	        for s in segs:
266	            s["mode"] = self.base_mode
267	        i = 0
268	        while i < len(segs):
269	            m = cand[i]
270	            if not m:
271	                i += 1
272	                continue
273	            j = i                                            # extend while the same mood keeps recurring
274	            while j + 1 < len(segs) and (cand[j + 1] == m or (j + 2 < len(segs) and cand[j + 2] == m)):
275	                j += 1
276	            total = sum(dur(segs[k]) + segs[k].get("freeze_end", 0) for k in range(i, j + 1))
277	            is_ending = j >= len(segs) - 2
278	            if total >= 8.0 or (m == "sad" and is_ending and total >= 2.0):
279	                if m == "sad" and is_ending:
280	                    j = len(segs) - 1                         # a sad ending stays sad to the last frame
281	                for k in range(i, j + 1):
282	                    segs[k]["mode"] = m
283	            i = j + 1

286	    def seg_of(self, segs: list[dict], t: float) -> dict | None:
287	        return next((s for s in segs if s["in"] <= t < s["out"] + 1e-6 and not s["id"].startswith("cold")), None)

290	    def plan(self) -> dict:
291	        beats = self.beats()
292	        segs = self.segments(beats)
293	        self.assign_modes(segs, beats)
294	        overlays, texts, sfx, emphasis = [], [], [], set()
295	        last = {"sfx": -9.0, "text": -9.0, "meme": -60.0, "gs": -60.0}
296	        duration = sum(seg_duration(s) for s in segs)
297	        self.n_sfx, self.max_sfx = 0, max(6, int(duration / 60 * 14))   # ~14 beat SFX per minute, max
298	        meme_budget = max(1, int(duration / 40))
299	        gs_budget = max(1, int(duration / 50))
300	        cutaways: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []                # (after seg id, cutaway seg)
301	
302	        for b in sorted(beats, key=lambda b: -b["score"]):   # strongest beats claim resources first
303	            s = self.seg_of(segs, b["t"])
304	            if not s:
305	                continue
306	            r = TREAT.get(b["moment"], {})
307	            mode = self.modes.get(s["mode"], {})
308	            zi = mode.get("zoom", {}).get("intensity", 1.0)
309	            if b["keyword"]:
310	                emphasis.add(b["keyword"])
311	            if r.get("zoom") and b["score"] >= 3 and s.get("speed", 1) == 1:
312	                to = 1 + (r["zoom"] - 1) * zi
313	                s.setdefault("zoom", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "to": round(to, 3), "in": 0.06,
314	                                                 "hold": max(0.4, b["end"] - b["t"] + 0.3), "out": 0.15})
315	            if r.get("shake") and mode.get("shake", 1) > 0:
316	                s.setdefault("shake", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "dur": 0.45,
317	                                                  "amp": round(r["shake"] * mode.get("shake", 1))})
318	            if r.get("sfx") and abs(b["t"] - last["sfx"]) > 4.0 and self.n_sfx < self.max_sfx:
319	                moments, roles = r["sfx"]
320	                a = self.pick(moments + mode.get("sfx_moments", [])[:1], roles,
321	                              categories=["sfx_meme", "sfx_ui", "sfx_minecraft", "sfx_mlg", "sfx_laugh"],
322	                              max_duration=6)
323	                if a:
324	                    hit = "hit" in a.get("roles", [])
325	                    # impacts land on the word; reactions/stingers right AFTER it (never on the punchline)
326	                    t = b["t"] if hit else b["end"] + 0.1
327	                    if self.seg_of(segs, t) is s:
328	                        ev = {"asset": a["id"], "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(t, 3),
329	                              "align": "peak" if hit else "onset", "_beat": b["moment"]}
330	                        cap = sfx_cap(a)
331	                        if cap:
332	                            ev["dur"] = cap
333	                        sfx.append(ev)
334	                        self.n_sfx += 1
335	                        last["sfx"] = b["t"]
336	            mg = self.motion_beat(b, s, overlays)
337	            recent_same = any(t["text"] == b.get("text") and abs(t.get("src_at", -99) - b["t"]) < 30 for t in texts)
338	            if b.get("text") and abs(b["t"] - last["text"]) > 3.5 and not recent_same and not mg:
339	                texts.append({"text": b["text"], "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "dur": 1.1,
340	                              "y": 0.32, **({"style": "minecraft"} if b["moment"] == "loot" else {})})
341	                last["text"] = b["t"]
342	            if r.get("meme") and meme_budget and b["score"] >= 3 and abs(b["t"] - last["meme"]) > 25 \
343	                    and s["out"] - b["end"] < 1.5:
344	                a = self.pick(r["meme"], categories=["meme_video"], max_duration=12, max_rating="clean")
345	                if a:
346	                    lo, hi = meme_window(a, self.rng)
347	                    cutaways.append((s["id"], {"id": f"meme-{len(cutaways) + 1}", "type": "cutaway",
348	                                               "asset": a["id"], "in": lo, "out": round(hi, 2)}))
349	                    meme_budget -= 1
350	                    last["meme"] = b["t"]
351	            if r.get("greenscreen") and gs_budget and not b.get("death_screen") and abs(b["t"] - last["gs"]) > 30 \
352	                    and b["score"] >= 4 and b.get("phrase"):
353	                a = self.pick(r["greenscreen"], categories=["green_screen"], max_duration=10, max_rating="clean")
354	                if a and (a.get("moments") or [None])[0] not in r["greenscreen"]:
355	                    a = None                                     # only overlays made FOR this kind of moment
356	                if a:
357	                    full = a.get("placement") == "fullscreen"
358	                    overlays.append({"type": "greenscreen", "asset": a["id"], "seg": s["id"],
359	                                     "src_at": round(b["end"], 3), "dur": min(3.0, a["duration_s"]),
360	                                     **({} if full else {"x": 0.78, "y": 0.62, "scale": 0.5})})
361	                    gs_budget -= 1
362	                    last["gs"] = b["t"]
363	            self.sticker_beat(b, s, overlays, mg or abs(b["t"] - last["meme"]) < 0.01 or abs(b["t"] - last["gs"]) < 0.01,
364	                              duration)
365	            if b["moment"] == "death" and b.get("death_screen"):
366	                s["freeze_end"] = max(s.get("freeze_end", 0), 1.6)
367	                s.setdefault("zoom", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"] + 0.05, 3), "to": 1.35, "in": 1.4,

369	                s["mode"] = "sad"

371	        # running gag: a content word said 4+ times within 45 s gets a counter ("STICKS x1", "x2", ...)
372	        for word, times in running_gags(self.words).items():
373	            for n, (t, seg_t) in enumerate(times, 1):
374	                s = self.seg_of(segs, t)

404	            a = max(0.0, top["t"] - 1.2)
405	            z = top["end"] + 0.8

409	            if ds:
410	                lead.append({"id": "cold-2", "type": "source", "in": round(ds["t"] - 0.05, 3),

412	                             "zoom": [{"src_at": round(ds["t"], 3), "to": 1.35, "in": 0.3, "focus": [0.5, 0.22]}]})
413	            first_src = next((s["in"] for s in segs if s["type"] == "source"), 0)

467	    def sticker_beat(self, b: dict, s: dict, overlays: list, busy: bool, duration: float) -> None:
468	        """The channel mascot reacts: a Crodie emote pops in a corner on a big beat (crying on a death, screaming
469	        on a jumpscare, heart eyes on loot). Sparse: strong beats only, >=25 s apart, ~1 per 40 s, never on a beat
470	        that already got a meme / green screen / game-UI graphic. A death screen is the payoff: it always gets the
471	        crying reaction, and the panic right before it stays clean so the two don't stack."""
472	        if busy or b["score"] < 4 or b["moment"] not in self.STICKER_MOMENTS:
473	            return
474	        deaths = [d["t"] for d in self.sig.get("death_screens", [])]
475	        if not b.get("death_screen") and any(0 < d - b["t"] < 15 for d in deaths):
476	            return                                       # leave the build-up clean for the death payoff
477	        ts = self.mg_used.setdefault("sticker_pop", [])
478	        if not b.get("death_screen") and (len(ts) >= max(1, min(5, int(duration / 40)))
479	                                          or any(abs(b["t"] - t) < 25 for t in ts)):
480	            return
481	        q = A.Query(moments=[b["moment"]], roles=["emotes"], categories=["brand_sticker"], project=self.slug,
482	                    exclude=self.used, limit=8, seed=self.rng.randint(0, 10 ** 6))
483	        res = [a for a in A.find(q) if b["moment"] in (a.get("moments") or [])]
484	        made_for = [a for a in res if a["moments"][0] == b["moment"]]   # emotes drawn FOR this moment first
485	        pool = (made_for or res)[:3]
486	        if not pool:
487	            return
488	        a = pool[0] if len(pool) == 1 or self.rng.random() < 0.6 else self.rng.choice(pool)
489	        self.used.append(a["id"])
490	        ts.append(b["t"])
491	        badge = a["id"].startswith("crodie.badge_")
492	        at = b["t"] + 0.6 if b.get("death_screen") else b["end"] + 0.1
493	        overlays.append({"type": "motion", "template": "sticker_pop", "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(at, 3),
494	                         "vars": {"image": a["path"],                     # studio-relative (brand/crodie/...)
495	                                  "position": "center" if badge else ("top-right" if len(ts) % 2 else "top-left"),
496	                                  "style": "stamp" if badge else "pop"},
497	                         **({"dur": 2.2} if b.get("death_screen") else {})})

499	    def motion_beat(self, b: dict, s: dict, overlays: list) -> bool:
500	        """Game-UI motion graphics for beats that literally match them. Sparing by design: each template has a
501	        per-video cap and a minimum gap, and only fires on a clear spoken trigger (creator: no overuse)."""
502	        kw = (b.get("phrase") or b.get("keyword") or "").lower()
503	        used = self.mg_used
504	        def ok(name, cap, gap):
505	            ts = used.setdefault(name, [])
506	            return len(ts) < cap and all(abs(b["t"] - t) > gap for t in ts)
507	        ov = None
508	        if b["moment"] == "loot" and b["score"] >= 4 and ok("advancement_toast", 2, 40):
509	            ov = {"template": "advancement_toast", "vars": {"title": kw.title().rstrip("!") + "!", "kind": "task"}}
510	        elif b["moment"] == "location" and ok("location_tag", 2, 60):
511	            ov = {"template": "location_tag",
512	                  "vars": {"text": kw.upper(), "sub": "", "icon": LOCATION_ICON.get(kw, "compass")}}
513	        elif b["moment"] == "boss" and ok("boss_bar", 1, 0):
514	            ov = {"template": "boss_bar", "vars": {"name": kw.title().replace("The ", ""),
515	                                                    "color": BOSS_COLOR.get(kw, "pink")}}
516	        if not ov:
517	            return False
518	        used[ov["template"]].append(b["t"])
519	        overlays.append({"type": "motion", **ov, "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(b["end"] + 0.05, 3)})
520	        return True

532	        """A bed per *music family* run. Beds only change for runs >= 12 s (mood blips don't swap songs);
533	        a short sad/death ending gets silence so the sting lands."""
534	        t = 0.0
535	        runs: list[list] = []                                # [family, start, end]
536	        for s in edl["segments"]:

540	                continue
541	            f = self.FAMILY.get(s.get("mode") or edl["mode"], "funny") if s["type"] != "cutaway" \
542	                else (runs[-1][0] if runs else "funny")
543	            if runs and runs[-1][0] == f:

546	                runs.append([f, t, t + d])

575	def running_gags(words: list[dict], min_count: int = 4, window: float = 45.0) -> dict[str, list]:
576	    """Content words repeated a lot in a short span - the editor's classic counter gag."""
577	    occ: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
578	    for w in words:
579	        k = re.sub(r"[^a-z']", "", w["word"].lower())
580	        if len(k) >= 4 and k not in STOP:
581	            occ.setdefault(k.rstrip("s") if k.endswith("s") and len(k) > 4 else k, []).append(w["start"])
582	    gags = {}
583	    for k, ts in occ.items():
584	        best: list[float] = []
585	        for i in range(len(ts)):
586	            run = [t for t in ts[i:] if t - ts[i] <= window]
587	            if len(run) > len(best):
588	                best = run
589	        if len(best) >= min_count:
590	            gags[k + ("s" if any(re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", w["word"].lower()) == k + "s" for w in words) else "")] = \
591	                [(t, t) for t in best[:10]]
592	    ranked = sorted(gags.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1]))
593	    # one gag per video; a second only if it's just as strong (6+ repeats)
594	    return dict(ranked[:1] + [kv for kv in ranked[1:2] if len(kv[1]) >= 6])

597	def meme_window(a: dict, rng) -> tuple[float, float]:
598	    """Use a meme for its comedic beat, not its whole runtime: short clips play in full, longer ones get a
599	    1.4-2.8 s window around their peak (or inside the tagged use_window). Not a strict rule - variety on purpose."""
600	    lo = a.get("use_in") or 0.0
601	    hi = a.get("use_out") or a.get("duration_s") or 2.0
602	    if hi - lo <= 3.5 and rng.random() < 0.7:
603	        return round(lo, 2), round(hi, 2)
604	    length = rng.uniform(1.4, 2.8)
605	    peak = a.get("peak_s")
606	    start = max(lo, min((peak - 0.6) if peak is not None else lo, hi - length))

634	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ engagement pass
635	def engage(edl: dict, words: list[dict], modes: dict) -> int:
636	    """Keep attention: no stretch longer than the mode's every_s without a visual change.
637	
638	    * consecutive talking segments alternate 1.0x / 1.1x framing, so jump cuts read as deliberate
639	    * gaps get a punch-in on the most stressed word (longest word or one ending in ! / ?),
640	      or a slow push-in when there is no good word
641	    Auto zooms carry "auto": true and are replaced on re-run; hand-placed zooms are never touched.
642	    """
643	    added = 0
644	    segs = edl["segments"]
645	    prev_reframed = False
646	    for i, s in enumerate(segs):
647	        if s.get("type", "source") != "source" or s.get("speed", 1) > 1:
648	            prev_reframed = False
649	            continue
650	        s["zoom"] = [z for z in s.get("zoom", []) if not z.get("auto")]
651	        mode = modes.get(s.get("mode") or edl.get("mode", "funny"), {})
652	        every = mode.get("zoom", {}).get("every_s", 3.5)
653	        inten = mode.get("zoom", {}).get("intensity", 1.0)
654	        snap = mode.get("zoom", {}).get("snap", True)
655	        live = s["out"] - s["in"]
656	        adjacent = i > 0 and segs[i - 1].get("type", "source") == "source" and abs(segs[i - 1]["out"] - s["in"]) < 2.5
657	        if adjacent and not prev_reframed and not s["id"].startswith("cold"):
658	            s["zoom"].insert(0, {"at": 0.0, "to": round(1 + 0.1 * inten, 3), "in": 0, "out": 0, "auto": True})
659	            prev_reframed = True
660	            added += 1
661	        else:
662	            prev_reframed = False
663	        # find gaps between existing changes inside the segment
664	        marks = sorted([0.0, live] + [(z["src_at"] - s["in"]) if "src_at" in z else z.get("at", 0)
665	                                      for z in s["zoom"] if not (z.get("auto") and z.get("at") == 0.0)])
666	        for a, b in zip(marks, marks[1:]):
667	            t = a + every
668	            while t < b - 0.8:
669	                cand = [w for w in words if s["in"] + t - every * 0.5 <= w["start"] <= s["in"] + min(b - 0.6, t + every * 0.5)]
670	                if cand:
671	                    w = max(cand, key=lambda w: (w["word"].endswith(("!", "?")), w["end"] - w["start"]))
672	                    at = w["start"] - s["in"]
673	                    if snap:
674	                        z = {"src_at": round(w["start"], 3), "to": round(1 + 0.2 * inten, 3), "in": 0.05,
675	                             "hold": round(max(0.4, w["end"] - w["start"] + 0.25), 2), "out": 0.15, "auto": True}
676	                    else:
677	                        z = {"src_at": round(w["start"], 3), "to": round(1 + 0.12 * inten, 3), "in": 1.2,
678	                             "hold": 0.6, "out": 0.6, "auto": True}
679	                else:
680	                    at = t
681	                    z = {"at": round(t, 3), "to": round(1 + 0.1 * inten, 3), "in": min(2.0, b - t), "out": 0.3,
682	                         "auto": True}
683	                s["zoom"].append(z)
684	                added += 1
685	                t = at + every
686	        if not s["zoom"]:
687	            s.pop("zoom")
688	    return added

190	def measure_voice(ctx: "Ctx") -> float:
191	    import numpy as np
192	    path, stream, offset, _ = voice_source(ctx)
193	    cache = ctx.proj / "work" / "levels.json"
194	    tr_p = ctx.proj / "work" / "transcript.json"
195	    chain = ctx.style["audio"]["mix"]["voice_chain"]
196	    key = f"v2|{path}|{stream}|{offset}|{path.stat().st_mtime:.0f}|{chain}"
197	    if tr_p.exists():
198	        key += f"|{tr_p.stat().st_mtime:.0f}"
199	    try:
200	        c = json.loads(cache.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
201	        if c.get("key") == key:
202	            return c["voice_db"] + ctx.style["audio"]["mic_db"]
203	    except (OSError, ValueError):
204	        pass
205	    sr = 8000
206	    # measure the voice AFTER its processing chain - that's what the SFX sit against in the mix
207	    raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(path), "-map", f"0:a:{stream}", "-af", chain,
208	                          "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(sr), "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True).stdout
209	    x = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
210	    mask = np.zeros(len(x), bool)
211	    if tr_p.exists():
212	        for seg in json.loads(tr_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"]:
213	            for w in seg.get("words", []):
214	                a, b = int((w["start"] + offset) * sr), int((w["end"] + offset) * sr)
215	                mask[max(0, a):max(0, b)] = True
216	    if mask.sum() > sr:          # more than 1 s of words
217	        v = x[mask]
218	        method = "transcript words"
219	    else:                        # fallback: loudest 30% of 100 ms windows
220	        n = len(x) // 800
221	        win = x[: n * 800].reshape(n, 800)
222	        r = (win ** 2).mean(axis=1)
223	        v = win[r >= np.percentile(r, 70)].ravel()
224	        method = "loudest 30% windows"
225	    # same metric as the catalog's loud_db: 90th percentile of 100 ms window loudness
226	    n = len(v) // 800
227	    win = v[: n * 800].reshape(n, 800)
228	    lvl = float(np.percentile(20 * np.log10(np.sqrt((win ** 2).mean(axis=1)) + 1e-9), 90))
229	    cache.write_text(json.dumps({"key": key, "voice_db": round(lvl, 2), "method": method}), encoding="utf-8")
230	    return lvl + ctx.style["audio"]["mic_db"]

234	def voice_envelope(ctx: "Ctx"):
235	    """10 ms RMS envelope (dB) of the voice track, cached per recording."""
236	    import numpy as np
237	    path, stream, offset, _ = voice_source(ctx)
238	    cache = ctx.proj / "work" / "voice_env.npz"
239	    key = f"{path}|{stream}|{offset}|{path.stat().st_mtime:.0f}"
240	    if cache.exists():
241	        z = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=False)
242	        if str(z["key"]) == key:
243	            return z["env"], float(z["offset"])
244	    sr = 8000
245	    raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(path), "-map", f"0:a:{stream}", "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(sr),
246	                          "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True).stdout
247	    x = np.frombuffer(raw, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
248	    n = len(x) // 80
249	    env = 20 * np.log10(np.sqrt((x[: n * 80].reshape(n, 80) ** 2).mean(axis=1)) + 1e-9).astype(np.float32)
250	    np.savez(cache, env=env, key=np.array(key), offset=np.array(offset))
251	    return env, offset

254	def guard_cuts(ctx: "Ctx") -> list[str]:
255	    """ASR word timestamps end early (trailing consonants, breath, room decay), so a cut placed on a
256	    word's end clips it. For every source segment: push the OUT point forward until the voice has really
257	    decayed (max 0.35 s) and pull the IN point back to the true onset (max 0.2 s). Never overlaps the
258	    neighbouring segment's footage; a segment with "exact": true is left alone."""
259	    import numpy as np
260	    try:
261	        env, offset = voice_envelope(ctx)
262	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
263	        return [f"cut guard skipped: {e}"]
264	    if env.size < 100:
265	        return []
266	    floor = float(np.percentile(env, 20))
267	    thr = max(floor + 9.0, ctx.voice_ref - 32.0)           # "still talking" if above this
268	    fps = 100.0
269	    idx = lambda t: int((t + offset) * fps)                 # noqa: E731  source time -> envelope index
270	    segs = ctx.edl["segments"]
271	    notes = []
272	    for i, s in enumerate(segs):
273	        if s.get("type", "source") != "source" or s.get("exact") or s.get("speed", 1.0) != 1.0:
274	            continue
275	        # neighbours in SOURCE time we must not run into (jump cuts of adjacent material)
276	        nxt_in = min((o["in"] for o in segs if o.get("type", "source") == "source" and o is not s
277	                      and o["in"] >= s["out"] - 1e-3 and o["in"] - s["out"] < 1.0), default=None)
278	        prv_out = max((o["out"] for o in segs if o.get("type", "source") == "source" and o is not s
279	                       and o["out"] <= s["in"] + 1e-3 and s["in"] - o["out"] < 1.0), default=None)
280	        out, k = s["out"], idx(s["out"])
281	        limit = out + 0.35 if nxt_in is None else min(out + 0.35, nxt_in)
282	        if 0 <= k < env.size and env[max(0, k - 3):k + 1].max() > thr:   # voice still going at the cut
283	            j = k
284	            quiet = 0
285	            while j < env.size and j / fps - offset < limit:
286	                quiet = quiet + 1 if env[j] <= thr else 0
287	                if quiet >= 6:                                 # 60 ms of real quiet = speech ended
288	                    break
289	                j += 1
290	            new_out = min(limit, max(out, (j - quiet + 3) / fps - offset))
291	            if new_out - out > 0.02:
292	                notes.append(f"{s.get('id', i)}: out +{new_out - out:.2f}s (word tail)")
293	                s["out"] = round(new_out, 3)
294	        inn, k = s["in"], idx(s["in"])
295	        lo = inn - 0.2 if prv_out is None else max(inn - 0.2, prv_out)
296	        if 0 <= k < env.size and env[k:k + 4].max() > thr:
297	            j = k
298	            while j > 0 and (j - 1) / fps - offset > lo and env[j - 1] > thr:
299	                j -= 1
300	            new_in = max(lo, j / fps - offset - 0.03)
301	            if inn - new_in > 0.02:
302	                d = inn - new_in
303	                notes.append(f"{s.get('id', i)}: in -{d:.2f}s (word onset)")
304	                s["in"] = round(new_in, 3)
305	                for z in s.get("zoom", []) + s.get("shake", []):   # segment-relative anchors keep their place
306	                    if "at" in z:
307	                        z["at"] = round(z["at"] + d, 3)
308	    return notes

312	def fit_filter(W: int, H: int, FPS: int, blur_bg: bool = True) -> str:
313	    """Letterbox anything into WxH; blurred cover background instead of black bars."""
314	    if not blur_bg:

355	def facecam_layout(ctx: Ctx, seg: dict) -> dict | None:
356	    if not ctx.facecam or seg.get("facecam") is False:
357	        return None
358	    fc = ctx.facecam
359	    vertical = ctx.format == "vertical"
360	    layout = fc.get("layout") or ("stack" if vertical else "corner")
361	    if layout == "stack" and vertical:
362	        fh = int(ctx.H * fc.get("ratio", 0.38)) // 2 * 2
363	        return {"layout": "stack", "fw": ctx.W, "fh": fh, "gw": ctx.W, "gh": ctx.H - fh}
364	    fw = int(ctx.W * fc.get("size", 0.42 if vertical else 0.24)) // 2 * 2
365	    fh = int(fw * 9 / 16) // 2 * 2 if not fc.get("square") else fw
366	    return {"layout": "corner", "fw": fw, "fh": fh, "gw": ctx.W, "gh": ctx.H}

369	def source_segment_filter(ctx: Ctx, seg: dict, game_has_audio: bool, mic_input: bool,
370	                          fc_index: int | None = None) -> tuple[str, float]:
371	    FPS = ctx.FPS
372	    fcl = facecam_layout(ctx, seg) if fc_index is not None else None
373	    # the gameplay "area" is the whole frame, unless a stacked facecam takes the top of a short
374	    W, H = (fcl["gw"], fcl["gh"]) if fcl else (ctx.W, ctx.H)
375	    speed = seg.get("speed", 1.0)
376	    live = (seg["out"] - seg["in"]) / speed
377	    vs = ctx.sources.get("game", {}).get("video_stream", 0)
378	    if ctx.format == "vertical":
379	        # fill the tall frame: Minecraft action lives at the crosshair, so a centred crop works;
380	        # `frame_x` (0..1) pans the crop when the action is off-centre
381	        fx0 = seg.get("frame_x", 0.5)
382	        fit = [f"scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase", f"crop={W}:{H}:(iw-{W})*{fx0}:(ih-{H})/2"]
383	    else:
384	        fit = [f"scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease", f"pad={W}:{H}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"]
385	    chain = [f"setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{speed}", f"fps={FPS}", *fit, "setsar=1"]
386	    mode = ctx.mode(seg)
387	
388	    # zoom + shake -> one dynamic scale + crop
389	    zterms, fxterms, fyterms, shake_x, shake_y = [], [], [], [], []
390	    for z in seg.get("zoom", []):
391	        a = z["at"] if "at" in z else (z["src_at"] - seg["in"]) / speed
392	        ri, ro = z.get("in", 0.12), z.get("out", 0.18)
393	        hold = z.get("hold", max(0.0, live - a - ri - ro))
394	        env = envelope(a, ri, hold, ro)
395	        zterms.append(f"{z.get('to', 1.3) - 1:.4f}*{env}")
396	        fx, fy = z.get("focus", [0.5, 0.5])
397	        fxterms.append(f"{fx - 0.5:.4f}*{env}")
398	        fyterms.append(f"{fy - 0.5:.4f}*{env}")
399	    for s in seg.get("shake", []):
400	        a = s["at"] if "at" in s else (s["src_at"] - seg["in"]) / speed
401	        amp = s.get("amp", 14) * H / 1080
402	        freq = s.get("freq", 18)
403	        env = envelope(a, 0.02, s.get("dur", 0.4), 0.1)
404	        zterms.append(f"{2.4 * amp / H:.5f}*{env}")
405	        shake_x.append(f"{amp:.2f}*sin({2 * math.pi * freq:.3f}*t)*{env}")
406	        shake_y.append(f"{amp * 0.8:.2f}*cos({2 * math.pi * freq * 1.3:.3f}*t)*{env}")
407	    if zterms:
408	        Z = "(1+" + "+".join(zterms) + ")"
409	        fx = "(0.5+" + "+".join(fxterms or ["0"]) + ")"
410	        fy = "(0.5+" + "+".join(fyterms or ["0"]) + ")"
411	        sx = "+".join(shake_x) or "0"
412	        sy = "+".join(shake_y) or "0"
413	        zw, zh = f"trunc({W}*{Z}/2)*2", f"trunc({H}*{Z}/2)*2"
414	        chain.append(f"scale=w='{zw}':h='{zh}':eval=frame")
415	        # crop's iw/ih keep the *initial* input size even when the frame grows, so derive the
416	        # scaled size from Z(t) directly - otherwise every zoom anchors to the top-left corner
417	        chain.append(f"crop={W}:{H}:x='max(0,min({zw}-{W},({zw}-{W})*{fx}+{sx}))'"
418	                     f":y='max(0,min({zh}-{H},({zh}-{H})*{fy}+{sy}))'")
419	    look = ctx.looks.get(seg.get("look") or ctx.look, {}).get("filter", "")
420	    if look:                                    # subtle always-on enhancement, under the mode grade
421	        chain.append(look)
422	    if mode.get("grade"):
423	        chain.append(mode["grade"])
424	    if mode.get("letterbox") and ctx.format != "vertical":
425	        bar = int(H * 0.105)
426	        chain.append(f"drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill,drawbox=x=0:y=ih-{bar}:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill")
427	    for e in seg.get("effects", []):
428	        if e not in EFFECTS:
429	            ctx.warnings.append(f"segment {seg.get('id')}: unknown effect {e!r}")
430	            continue
431	        chain.append(EFFECTS[e](ctx))
432	    freeze = seg.get("freeze_end", 0.0)
433	    total = live + freeze
434	    tail = (f",tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration={freeze:.3f}" if freeze else "") + ",format=yuv420p"
435	    if not fcl:
436	        fc = f"[0:v:{vs}]" + ",".join(chain) + tail + "[v];"
437	    else:
438	        f = ctx.facecam
439	        fw, fh = fcl["fw"], fcl["fh"]
440	        crop = f.get("crop")                                   # normalised [x, y, w, h] to frame the face
441	        cropf = f"crop=iw*{crop[2]}:ih*{crop[3]}:iw*{crop[0]}:ih*{crop[1]}," if crop else ""
442	        flip = "hflip," if f.get("flip") else ""
443	        cam = (f"[{fc_index}:v]setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{speed},fps={FPS},{cropf}{flip}"
444	               f"scale={fw}:{fh}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={fw}:{fh},format=rgba")
445	        fc = f"[0:v:{vs}]" + ",".join(chain) + "[g];"
446	        if fcl["layout"] == "stack":
447	            line = f.get("border", "#5FBF3A").replace("#", "0x")
448	            fc += cam + "[cam];"
449	            fc += (f"[g]pad={ctx.W}:{ctx.H}:0:{fh}:color=black[gp];[gp][cam]overlay=0:0:shortest=1,"
450	                   f"drawbox=x=0:y={fh - 4}:w=iw:h=8:color={line}:t=fill{tail}[v];")
451	        else:
452	            r = int(fh * 0.14)
453	            b = max(2, int(f.get("border_px", 6) * ctx.H / 1080))
454	            mask = rounded_plate(ctx, fw, fh, r, None)
455	            plate = rounded_plate(ctx, fw + 2 * b, fh + 2 * b, r + b, f.get("border", "#5FBF3A"))
456	            cx, cy = f.get("x", 0.86 if ctx.format != "vertical" else 0.5), f.get("y", 0.2 if ctx.format != "vertical" else 0.14)
457	            fc += cam + "[cam];"
458	            fc += f"movie={mask}:loop=0,setpts=N/{FPS}/TB,format=gray[mask];[cam][mask]alphamerge[camr];"
459	            fc += f"movie={plate}:loop=0,setpts=N/{FPS}/TB,format=rgba[plate];"
460	            fc += f"[plate][camr]overlay={b}:{b}:shortest=1[camb];"
461	            fc += (f"[g][camb]overlay=x='{ctx.W * cx:.0f}-overlay_w/2':y='{ctx.H * cy:.0f}-overlay_h/2':"
462	                   f"eof_action=pass{tail}[v];")
463	
464	    aud = ctx.style["audio"]
465	    tempo = atempo_chain(speed)
466	    parts = []
467	    voice_in_game = voice_source(ctx)[3]
468	    if game_has_audio and not seg.get("mute_game"):
469	        # single mixed track (no separate mic): it IS the voice, so it gets mic level, not the game cut
470	        g_db = (aud["mic_db"] + seg.get("mic_db", 0)) if voice_in_game else \
471	            (aud["game_db"] + seg.get("game_db", 0) + mode.get("game_db_offset", 0))
472	        a_s = ctx.sources.get("game", {}).get("audio_stream", 0)
473	        parts.append(f"[0:a:{a_s}]" + ",".join(["asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS", f"volume={db(g_db)}", *tempo,
474	                                                 "aresample=48000", "aformat=channel_layouts=stereo"]) + "[ga]")
475	    if mic_input and not seg.get("mute_mic"):
476	        m_db = aud["mic_db"] + seg.get("mic_db", 0)
477	        m = ctx.sources["mic"]
478	        idx = "0" if m.get("file") in (None, ctx.sources["game"]["file"]) else "1"
479	        ms = m.get("stream", 0)
480	        parts.append(f"[{idx}:a:{ms}]" + ",".join(["asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS", f"volume={db(m_db)}", *tempo,
481	                                                  "aresample=48000", "aformat=channel_layouts=stereo"]) + "[ma]")
482	    labels = "".join(p[p.rindex("["):] for p in parts)
483	    if parts:
484	        fc += ";".join(parts) + ";"
485	        mix = f"{labels}amix=inputs={len(parts)}:normalize=0," if len(parts) > 1 else f"{labels}anull,"
486	        # 12 ms fades at both ends: jump cuts never click or pop
487	        fades = f"afade=t=in:d=0.012,afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, live - 0.012):.4f}:d=0.012,"
488	        fc += mix + fades + f"apad=whole_dur={total:.4f},atrim=0:{total:.4f}[a]"
489	    else:
490	        fc += f"anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo,atrim=0:{total:.4f}[a]"
491	    return fc, total

545	        fx = "".join("," + EFFECTS[e](ctx) for e in seg.get("effects", []) if e in EFFECTS)
546	        fc = f"[0:v]setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,{vf}{fx}{tail}[v];"
547	        total = dur + freeze
548	        vol = ctx.matched_db(a, ctx.style["audio"]["mix"]["cutaway_rel_db"], a.get("volume_db") or 0) \
549	            + seg.get("volume_db", 0)
550	        if has_audio and not seg.get("mute"):
551	            fc += (f"[0:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,volume={db(vol)},aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo,"
552	                   f"apad=whole_dur={total:.4f},atrim=0:{total:.4f}[a]")
553	        else:

555	    script = ctx.work / "segs" / f"{i:03d}.fc.txt"

558	             "-r", ctx.FPS, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", "-ar", 48000, out]
559	    run_ff(args, ctx.work, ctx.log)
560	    return out

564	def sfx_timing(ctx: Ctx, ev: dict, at: float) -> tuple[float, float, float | None]:
565	    """-> (place_at, source_in, duration) honouring alignment to the asset's hit point."""
566	    a = ctx.asset(ev["asset"]) if ev.get("asset") else {}
567	    align = ev.get("align") or ("peak" if "hit" in a.get("roles", []) else "onset")
568	    src_in = ev.get("in", a.get("use_in") if a.get("use_in") is not None else (a.get("onset_s") or 0.0))
569	    place = at
570	    if align == "peak" and a.get("peak_s") is not None:
571	        place = at - max(0.0, a["peak_s"] - src_in)
572	    dur = ev.get("dur")
573	    if dur is None and a.get("use_out"):
574	        dur = a["use_out"] - src_in
575	    if dur is None and a.get("tail_s"):
576	        dur = a["tail_s"] - src_in + 0.05
577	    return max(0.0, place), src_in, dur

580	def speech_gate_envelope(ctx: Ctx, spans, total: float) -> Path | None:
581	    """Single mixed track (voice + game on one track): write a gain envelope that keeps the track at
582	    full level while you talk and pulls it down to game level between words, so digging, damage and
583	    splash noises stop competing with the voice. Cutaway/card spans stay at full level."""
584	    import wave
585	
586	    import numpy as np
587	    if not voice_source(ctx)[3]:
588	        return None
589	    tr_p = ctx.proj / "work" / "transcript.json"
590	    g = ctx.style["audio"]["mix"].get("game_between_words_db")
591	    if g is None or not tr_p.exists():
592	        return None
593	    sr, pre, post, ramp = 1000, 0.12, 0.22, 0.06          # 1 kHz control rate is plenty for a gain curve
594	    n = int(total * sr) + 1
595	    floor = 10 ** (g / 20)
596	    env = np.full(n, floor, dtype=np.float32)
597	    for sp in spans:
598	        if sp.src_in is None:                              # meme cutaways keep their own audio untouched
599	            env[int(sp.out_start * sr):int(sp.out_end * sr)] = 1.0
600	    for seg in json.loads(tr_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"]:
601	        for w in seg.get("words", []):
602	            for sp in spans:
603	                a = sp.src_to_out(w["start"])
604	                if a is None:
605	                    continue
606	                b = sp.src_to_out(w["end"])
607	                b = min(b if b is not None else sp.out_end, sp.out_end)
608	                env[max(0, int((a - pre) * sr)):int(min(sp.out_end, b + post) * sr)] = 1.0
609	    k = max(1, int(ramp * sr))                             # smooth the edges (no clicks / pumping)
610	    env = np.convolve(env, np.ones(k) / k, mode="same").astype(np.float32)
611	    out = ctx.work / "speech_gate.wav"
612	    pcm = (np.clip(env, 0, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
613	    with wave.open(str(out), "wb") as wf:
614	        wf.setnchannels(1)
615	        wf.setsampwidth(2)
616	        wf.setframerate(sr)
617	        wf.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
618	    return out

621	def render_audio(ctx: Ctx, base: Path, overlay_audio: list[dict], spans, total: float) -> Path:
622	    aud = ctx.style["audio"]
623	    A_ = ctx.edl.get("audio", {})
624	    inputs: list[list] = [["-i", base]]
625	    chains, mix = [], []
626	
627	    # dialogue bus with bleeps
628	    bleeps = []
629	    for i, b in enumerate(A_.get("bleeps", [])):
630	        at = resolve_time(b, spans, ctx.warnings, f"bleep[{i}]")
631	        if at is not None:
632	            bleeps.append((at, b.get("dur", 0.4)))
633	    mxcfg = aud["mix"]
634	    gate = speech_gate_envelope(ctx, spans, total)
635	    if gate:
636	        inputs.append(["-i", gate])
637	        chains.append(f"[{len(inputs) - 1}:a]aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo[gate]")
638	        chains.append("[0:a]aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo[dry]")
639	        dlg = "[dry][gate]amultiply," + mxcfg["voice_chain"]
640	    else:
641	        dlg = "[0:a]aresample=48000," + mxcfg["voice_chain"]
642	    for at, d in bleeps:
643	        dlg += f",volume=0:enable='between(t,{at:.3f},{at + d:.3f})'"
644	    music = A_.get("music", [])
645	    n_duck = sum(1 for m in music if m.get("duck", True))
646	    # sidechain keys: one per ducked music track + one for the SFX bus
647	    dlg += f",asplit={n_duck + 2}[dlg][sfxkey]" + "".join(f"[key{k}]" for k in range(n_duck))
648	    chains.append(dlg)
649	    mix.append("[dlg]")
650	    sfx_bus: list[str] = []
651	    for k, (at, d) in enumerate(bleeps):
652	        chains.append(f"sine=f={aud['bleep_hz']}:d={d:.3f}:r=48000,volume={db(aud['bleep_db'])},"
653	                      f"aformat=channel_layouts=stereo,adelay=delays={int(at * 1000)}:all=1[bl{k}]")
654	        mix.append(f"[bl{k}]")
655	
656	    def add_clip(path: Path, place: float, src_in: float, dur: float | None, vol: float, label: str, loop=False,
657	                 natural: float | None = None):
658	        n = len(inputs)
659	        inp = (["-stream_loop", "-1"] if loop else []) + ["-ss", f"{src_in:.4f}"]
660	        if dur:
661	            inp += ["-t", f"{dur:.4f}"]
662	        inputs.append(inp + ["-i", path])
663	        # a sound cut before its natural end fades out instead of stopping dead
664	        fade = f",afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, dur - 0.14):.3f}:d=0.14" if dur and natural and dur < natural - 0.05 else ""
665	        chains.append(f"[{n}:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo{fade},"
666	                      f"volume={db(vol)},adelay=delays={int(place * 1000)}:all=1[{label}]")
667	        return label
668	
669	    for i, ev in enumerate(A_.get("sfx", [])):
670	        at = resolve_time(ev, spans, ctx.warnings, f"sfx[{i}] {ev.get('asset')}")
671	        if at is None:
672	            continue
673	        place, src_in, dur = sfx_timing(ctx, ev, at)
674	        a = ctx.asset(ev["asset"]) if ev.get("asset") else {}
675	        vol = ctx.matched_db(a, ctx.sfx_rel(a), aud["sfx_db"] + (a.get("volume_db") or 0)) + ev.get("volume_db", 0)
676	        natural = (a.get("tail_s") or a.get("duration_s") or 0) - src_in if a else None
677	        sfx_bus.append("[" + add_clip(ctx.media_path(ev), place, src_in, dur, vol, f"sfx{i}", natural=natural) + "]")
678	
679	    for j, oa in enumerate(overlay_audio):
680	        sfx_bus.append("[" + add_clip(oa["path"], oa["at"], oa["in"], oa["dur"], oa["vol"], f"ova{j}",
681	                                      natural=oa.get("natural")) + "]")
682	
683	    if sfx_bus:
684	        # SFX dip a few dB while you talk, so a sound never buries your words
685	        d = mxcfg["sfx_duck"]
686	        pre = "".join(sfx_bus) + (f"amix=inputs={len(sfx_bus)}:normalize=0" if len(sfx_bus) > 1 else "anull")
687	        chains.append(pre + "[sfxmix]")
688	        chains.append(f"[sfxmix][sfxkey]sidechaincompress=threshold={d['threshold']}:ratio={d['ratio']}:"
689	                      f"attack={d['attack']}:release={d['release']}[sfxbus]")
690	        mix.append("[sfxbus]")
691	    else:
692	        chains.append("[sfxkey]anullsink")
693	
694	    kidx = 0
695	    for i, m in enumerate(music):
696	        at = resolve_time(m, spans, ctx.warnings, f"music[{i}]") if ("at" in m or "src_at" in m or "seg" in m) else 0.0
697	        if at is None:
698	            continue
699	        until = m.get("until", total)
700	        dur = max(0.1, until - at)
701	        a = ctx.asset(m["asset"]) if m.get("asset") else {}
702	        vol = ctx.matched_db(a, mxcfg["music_rel_db"], aud["music_db"] + (a.get("volume_db") or 0)) \
703	            + m.get("volume_db", 0)
704	        n = len(inputs)
705	        inputs.append(["-stream_loop", "-1", "-ss", f"{m.get('in', 0.0):.3f}", "-i", ctx.media_path(m)])
706	        fi, fo = m.get("fade_in", 0.5), m.get("fade_out", 1.5)
707	        c = (f"[{n}:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{dur:.3f},"
708	             f"afade=t=in:d={fi},afade=t=out:st={max(0, dur - fo):.3f}:d={fo},volume={db(vol)},"
709	             f"adelay=delays={int(at * 1000)}:all=1")
710	        if m.get("duck", True):
711	            d = aud["duck"]
712	            chains.append(c + f"[mu{i}]")
713	            chains.append(f"[mu{i}][key{kidx}]sidechaincompress=threshold={d['threshold']}:ratio={d['ratio']}:"
714	                          f"attack={d['attack']}:release={d['release']}[mus{i}]")
715	            kidx += 1
716	        else:
717	            chains.append(c + f"[mus{i}]")
718	        mix.append(f"[mus{i}]")
719	
720	    chains.append("".join(mix) + f"amix=inputs={len(mix)}:normalize=0:duration=first,"
721	                  f"atrim=0:{total:.4f},alimiter=limit=0.97:level=false[premix]")
722	    script = ctx.work / "audio.fc.txt"
723	    script.write_text(";\n".join(chains), encoding="utf-8")
724	    premix = ctx.work / "premix.wav"
725	    flat = [x for inp in inputs for x in inp]
726	    run_ff([*flat, "-/filter_complex", script, "-map", "[premix]", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", premix], ctx.work, ctx.log)
727	
728	    # two-pass loudness normalisation to the YouTube target
729	    I, TP = aud["target_lufs"], aud["true_peak"]
730	    r = subprocess.run(FFMPEG[:-1] + ["-v", "info", "-i", str(premix), "-af",
731	                                      f"loudnorm=I={I}:TP={TP}:LRA=11:print_format=json", "-f", "null", "-"],
732	                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
733	    js = r.stderr[r.stderr.rfind("{"): r.stderr.rfind("}") + 1]
734	    mix_wav = ctx.work / "mix.wav"
735	    # Static gain to the target + a peak limiter. (loudnorm's own "linear" mode silently falls back to
736	    # dynamic compression when the true-peak ceiling can't be met, which drags SFX tails up toward
737	    # the voice and wrecks the voice/SFX balance set above.)
738	    try:
739	        gain = I - float(json.loads(js)["input_i"])
740	    except (ValueError, KeyError):
741	        ctx.warnings.append("loudness measurement failed; no gain applied")
742	        gain = 0.0
743	    limit = 10 ** (TP / 20)
744	    af = f"volume={gain:.2f}dB,alimiter=limit={limit:.4f}:attack=3:release=60:level=false,aresample=48000"
745	    run_ff(["-i", premix, "-af", af, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", mix_wav], ctx.work, ctx.log)
746	    return mix_wav

751	    sim, blend = ev.get("similarity", 0.16), ev.get("blend", 0.08)

782	def avatar_overlays(ctx: Ctx, spans, cur: str, chains: list[str]) -> str:
783	    """Talking narrator avatar for every run of segments whose mode has avatar_on (narration), any
784	    segment with "avatar": true, or everything when edl.avatar.always. Mouth flaps follow the transcript;
785	    the expression follows the mode (sad -> sad face, scary -> shocked, ...).
786	
787	    The whole avatar performance is pre-rendered ONCE as a single transparent ProRes track (concat of
788	    timed state images), then composited with one overlay - cost doesn't grow with narration length."""
789	    import hashlib as _h
790	
791	    from PIL import Image
792	
793	    from . import avatar as AV
794	    adir = STUDIO / "brand" / "avatar"
795	    if not (adir / "idle.png").exists():
796	        return cur
797	    cfg = ctx.edl.get("avatar", {})
798	    runs: list[dict] = []
799	    for sp in spans:
800	        seg = ctx.edl["segments"][sp.seg_index]
801	        m = ctx.mode(seg)
802	        if not seg.get("avatar", cfg.get("always", False) or m.get("avatar_on", False)):
803	            continue
804	        mood = seg.get("avatar_mood") or cfg.get("mood") or m.get("avatar") or "neutral"
805	        end = sp.out_end + seg.get("freeze_end", 0.0)
806	        if runs and abs(runs[-1]["end"] - sp.out_start) < 0.06:
807	            if runs[-1]["mood"] == mood:
808	                runs[-1]["end"] = end
809	                continue
810	            runs[-1]["cont"] = True                     # mood change mid-run: no slide out/in
811	        runs.append({"start": sp.out_start, "end": end, "mood": mood})
812	    if not runs:
813	        return cur
814	    tr_p = ctx.proj / "work" / "transcript.json"
815	    words = []
816	    if tr_p.exists():
817	        for seg in json.loads(tr_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"]:
818	            for w in seg.get("words", []):
819	                for sp in spans:
820	                    a0 = sp.src_to_out(w["start"])
821	                    if a0 is None:
822	                        continue
823	                    b0 = sp.src_to_out(w["end"])
824	                    words.append({"word": w["word"], "start": a0,
825	                                  "end": min(b0 if b0 is not None else sp.out_end, sp.out_end)})
826	    W, H, FPS = ctx.W, ctx.H, ctx.FPS
827	    vertical = ctx.format == "vertical"
828	    h = int(H * cfg.get("scale", 0.2 if vertical else 0.34)) // 2 * 2
829	    cx = W * cfg.get("x", 0.2 if vertical else 0.13)
830	    bottom = H * cfg.get("bottom", 0.8 if vertical else 1.0)
831	    stage = ctx.work / "stage"
832	    stage.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
833	
834	    def state_png(mood: str, variant: str) -> str:
835	        stem = AV.state_name(mood, "" if variant == "idle" else variant)
836	        if not (adir / f"{stem}.png").exists():
837	            stem = AV.state_name("neutral", "" if variant == "idle" else variant)
838	        src = adir / f"{stem}.png"
839	        dst = stage / f"av{h}_{stem}_{int(src.stat().st_mtime)}.png"     # rebuilt avatar -> new file
840	        if not dst.exists():
841	            im = Image.open(src).convert("RGBA")
842	            pixel = json.loads((adir / "avatar.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("kind") == "skin"                 if (adir / "avatar.json").exists() else True
843	            im = im.resize((int(im.width * h / im.height) // 2 * 2, h), Image.NEAREST if pixel else Image.LANCZOS)
844	            im.save(dst)
845	        return dst.name
846	
847	    blank = stage / f"av{h}_blank.png"
848	    if not blank.exists():
849	        ref = Image.open(stage / state_png("neutral", "idle"))
850	        Image.new("RGBA", ref.size, (0, 0, 0, 0)).save(blank)
851	    # timeline of (duration, image) across the whole video
852	    total = spans[-1].out_end + ctx.edl["segments"][spans[-1].seg_index].get("freeze_end", 0.0)
853	    items: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
854	    t = 0.0
855	    for r in runs:
856	        if r["start"] > t:
857	            items.append((r["start"] - t, blank.name))
858	        sched = AV.mouth_schedule([w for w in words if r["start"] <= w["start"] < r["end"]], fps=FPS,
859	                                  start=r["start"], end=r["end"])
860	        for a0, b0, st in sched:
861	            items.append((b0 - a0, state_png(r["mood"], st)))
862	        t = r["end"]
863	    if total > t:
864	        items.append((total - t, blank.name))
865	    listing = "ffconcat version 1.0\n" + "".join(f"file '{img}'\nduration {d:.4f}\n" for d, img in items if d > 0)
866	    listing += f"file '{items[-1][1]}'\n"
867	    key = _h.sha1((listing + str(FPS)).encode()).hexdigest()[:10]
868	    track = stage / f"avatar_{key}.mov"
869	    if not track.exists():
870	        lst = stage / f"avatar_{key}.txt"
871	        lst.write_text(listing, encoding="utf-8")
872	        run_ff(["-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", lst.name, "-vf", f"fps={FPS},format=yuva444p10le",
873	                "-c:v", "prores_ks", "-profile:v", "4444", "-t", f"{total:.3f}", track.name], stage, ctx.log)
874	    # slide up at the start of each run / down at its end, gentle bob
875	    terms = []
876	    for i, r in enumerate(runs):
877	        a0, z = r["start"], r["end"]
878	        if i == 0 or not runs[i - 1].get("cont"):
879	            terms.append(f"between(t,{a0:.3f},{a0 + 0.25:.3f})*(1-(t-{a0:.3f})/0.25)")
880	        if not r.get("cont"):
881	            terms.append(f"between(t,{z - 0.25:.3f},{z:.3f})*((t-{z - 0.25:.3f})/0.25)")
882	    slide = f"{h}*({'+'.join(terms) or '0'})"
883	    y = f"{bottom:.0f}-overlay_h+{slide}+{H * 0.004:.1f}*sin(2*PI*1.1*t)"
884	    chains.append(f"movie=stage/{track.name},setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,format=rgba[avtrack]")
885	    chains.append(f"{cur}[avtrack]overlay=x='{cx:.0f}-overlay_w/2':y='{y}':eof_action=pass[avo]")
886	    return "[avo]"
